title: Umami is the savory taste of glutamate
summary: Umami, often called savory, is the taste of the amino acid L-glutamate, and OpenStax counts it with sweet, salty, sour, and bitter.
body: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology says only four tastes were recognized until research led to a fifth, umami, in the mid-1980s. Umami is a Japanese word the book translates as delicious taste, often meaning savory. The receptor is activated by L-glutamate, so the flavor shows up in protein-rich foods. The chapter is CC BY 4.0. It also says very recent research has suggested a possible further taste for fats, which this card does not adopt as established.
